{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our playbook. The good news is that the risk-allocation architecture is largely acceptable as drafted: limitation of liability (§21), assignment and change of control (§24), licence grant (§13), audit rights (§22), auto-renewal and uplift caps (§8), warranties (§19) and Vendor insurance (§18) all meet our preferred positions and require no redline.

The problems are concentrated in two places. First, a cluster of one-sided commercial restraints binding us alone — a three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment with no reduction or exit right (§2.1), a disclose-and-match obligation before we may engage another provider (§7.2), a 24-month post-term non-compete, and a 24-month outright no-hire (both numbered §12.4). Each of these sits in walk-away territory, and each directly contradicts §12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. We read those restraints as inconsistent with the deal Vendor itself has papered, and we have proposed deletions or minimal negating edits accordingly.

Second, there are structural gaps and internal inconsistencies. There is **no indemnification article at all** — the outline jumps from §19 to §21 — yet §9.3, §19.4, §21.3 and §30.5 all cross-reference indemnities that do not exist, leaving §9.3's reference to "Section 20.5" broken. There is no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation, and §16.5 defers Customer Data to a "Section 11" that does not appear in the document. There is no termination-for-convenience right anywhere in a three-year term. Finally, §28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts while §28.2 confers exclusive jurisdiction on the New York County courts — an outright conflict that must be resolved in favour of New York.

One item requires attention before we send: the governing-law redline (§28.1/§28.2) failed verification and should be re-drafted internally rather than transmitted in its current form.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Compliant | §21.1 (with §§1.5, 21.2–21.4, 18.2) | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; full Excluded Claims set. No redline. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | §24.1 (with §§24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Free Customer assignment to Affiliate/successor on notice; Vendor restricted asymmetrically in our favour. No redline. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | **Deviation** | §7.2 (first clause so numbered) | De facto exclusivity/ROFR for the full term, no category limit, no 12-month cap, no performance exit. Conflicts with §12.3. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | §27.3 (with §§7.3, 24.4) | No Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination fee. No redline. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | §13.1 (with §§13.2–13.3, 14.3, 10.1) | Grant extends to Affiliates, contractors and Authorized Users; paid-up perpetual rights in Vendor Technology. No redline. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | §22.1 (with §§22.2–22.3) | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, no system or third-party data access. No redline. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | §8.2 (with §8.3) | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder with deadline extension; uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. No redline. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | §10.2 (and §16.5) | No transition assistance and no Customer Data return or certified deletion; §16.5 defers to a non-existent Section 11. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | §19.1 (with §§19.2–19.5, 6.2) | Workmanlike and conformity warranties; Hosted Services conform for the whole term; mutual, carved-back disclaimer. No redline. |
| Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | §28.1 (conflicting with §28.2) | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts — outside the accepted list — while §28.2 confers exclusive New York County jurisdiction. **Proposed redline failed verification.** |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | No §20; cross-referenced at §§9.3, 19.4, 21.3, 30.5 (see §19.5) | No indemnification article exists; §9.3's reference to "Section 20.5" is broken. Below fallback and in walk-away territory. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | §18.1 (with §18.2) | CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber and privacy 5M, workers' compensation, term plus one year. No redline. |
| Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | §14.2 (with §§13.2, 13.3, 14.3) | Vendor owns every Deliverable; our licence is revocable, non-transferable and term-limited. Fails the fallback. |
| Low | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | **Deviation** | §7.2 | Open-ended obligation to disclose and match better third-party offers; no product, term or comparison limits. Conflicts with §12.3. |
| Low | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | **Deviation** | §2.1 | Three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights". Conflicts with §12.3. |
| Low | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | **Deviation** | §12.4 (duplicate-numbered, p0046) | 24-month post-term ban on any competing product or service in any territory; no carve-outs. Conflicts with §12.3. |
| Low | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | **Deviation** | §12.4 | One-sided 24-month outright no-hire covering all Vendor employees, expressly negating advertising and unsolicited-application carve-outs. Conflicts with §12.3. |
| Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | §9.3 (no §9.4; with §§8.1, 2.1) | No Customer convenience right in a three-year term, compounded by the §2.1 take-or-pay. |

---

## Walk-away items

The following each sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than trading chips:

1. **Minimum commitment (§2.1).** A three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights. Our position: no committed minimum; Fees payable only for Services ordered or used. Fallback offered in comment: commitment confined to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, settled by true-up rather than penalty.
2. **Exclusivity / MFN (§7.2).** The disclose-and-match operator restrains our sourcing freedom for the whole term and simultaneously imposes an unlimited MFN. Our position: negate the operator so no exclusivity, sole-supplier or match obligation binds us. Note this clause is flagged under two rules because both are independently breached — the sourcing restraint and the MFN obligation.
3. **Non-compete (duplicate §12.4, p0046).** A 24-month post-term ban on any competing product or service in any territory. Our position: deletion, leaving §12.3 to govern. Fallback offered: a term-only restriction limited to a single named product.
4. **No-hire (§12.4).** One-sided, 24 months, all Vendor employees, with advertising and unsolicited-application carve-outs expressly negated. Our position: deletion. Fallback offered: mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to Services personnel, with customary carve-outs.
5. **No Vendor indemnity (no §20).** With no IP or law-compliance indemnity, and broken cross-references at §9.3, §19.4, §21.3 and §30.5, the Agreement falls below even the fallback. We have inserted a preferred Vendor defence/indemnity (third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breaches, gross negligence and wilful misconduct), procure/modify/replace/refund remedies at §20.5 restoring the §9.3 cross-reference, standard claim procedure, and a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and our own breach of law.
6. **No termination for convenience (§9).** A three-year term with only cause-based exits, reinforced by the §2.1 exclusion of termination rights. We have proposed a new §9.4 (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no Vendor convenience right during a committed term) with a conforming edit to §2.1.
7. **Exclusive foreign venue (§28.1).** Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts, in direct conflict with the New York County jurisdiction already conferred by §28.2.

---

## Next steps

1. **Re-draft the governing-law redline.** The proposed §28.1/§28.2 edit failed verification and should not be sent as drafted. The intended minimal fix is to change only the governing-law and forum words in §28.1 to New York law and the courts of New York County, aligning with §28.2, and to confine the §28.2 injunction carve-out to those courts. §28.3's escalation process is acceptable and unchanged.
2. **Raise the §12.3 inconsistency directly with Vendor.** §2.1, §7.2 and both §12.4 clauses each contradict Vendor's own acknowledgement in §12.3 that we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. We should ask Vendor to confirm which provision reflects the agreed deal; that framing should carry most of these deletions without protracted negotiation.
3. **Fix the numbering and cross-reference defects.** The document has no §20 and no §11, two clauses numbered §12.4, and two numbered §7.2, and §16.5 defers Customer Data to the non-existent §11. Ask Vendor to re-issue a clean, correctly numbered draft alongside its response so the inserted §9.4, §10.3 and §20 land cleanly.
4. **Confirm the exit package.** Press for the inserted §10.3 (up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, Customer Data returned in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter subject to routine backup and legal retention, consistent with §16.5). Given the volume of data at issue, we should not sign without a guaranteed retrieval path.
5. **Resolve Deliverable ownership (§14.2).** Our redline flips ownership with an assignment on creation while preserving Vendor's retention of generic tools, know-how and Vendor Technology under §14.3. Fallback to be conceded only if needed: a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, modifiable and sublicensable licence. Note the §13.2 perpetual licence covers only embedded Vendor Technology and does not cure this gap.
6. **Circulate the compliant list to the business.** §§13, 18, 19, 21, 22, 24 and the §8.2–8.3 renewal mechanic are at our preferred positions and should be protected from erosion in any Vendor counter-draft.

*This memo reflects only the verified findings supplied and does not address terms outside the scope of that review.*"}
